subject: Launchpad AI - Dedicated capacity sizing & safety-margin proposal
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Li <sara@launchpad.ai>, eng-ops@launchpad.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-10T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing — initial tokens/sec and safety margin proposal

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I put together an initial sizing note for the Launchpad dedicated pool you asked about. The two core asks you shared were:

- Steady-state interactive SLO: 95th percentile latency <= 250ms for 1k concurrent users (chat).
- Peak burst support for nightly batch reranks and a marketing spike (~4x baseline) with graceful degradation.

High-level proposal (summary):
- Model: open-llama-13B-q4f16 (redwood-verified profile)
- Baseline throughput estimate: 6.2 tokens/sec per GPU for typical chat sequences (avg seq len ~80 tokens, single-stream latency target)
- Per-instance effective TPS (multi-session batching): ~720 tokens/sec (assuming 8x virtual concurrency and 1.5× batching efficiency)
- Recommended committed slab: 8 GPUs for baseline (gives ~5.8k tokens/sec), with 4-GPU burst pool for 2x headroom and a 12-GPU soft cap for emergency bursts
- Safety margin: plan for 30–40% overhead for model variance, quantization delta, and KV cache fragmentation — we recommend final commit = baseline slab × 1.35 => 11 GPUs committed for a conservative SLA fit

I've attached the expected QPS CSV you sent and a one-page proposal PDF with the above math. Please confirm whether the average session token length we used (80) matches your telemetry, and whether there are other modeller variants you want us to test (we can rerun the microbenchmarks once we get your sample traces).

Next steps I propose:
1) You share a 48h sample of production traces (anonymized) or confirm avg tokens per session
2) We run a quick 24h replay on a dedicated 4-GPU test slab and report measured p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec
3) Agree on commit delta and formalize the reserved capacity quote

Thanks — happy to walk through the slide math if useful.

— Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Hi Kimberly —

Appreciate the clear breakdown. A few clarifications from our side:

- Avg tokens/session: 65 (interactive) with 95th at ~200 tokens. Nightly reranks are ~1.2M tokens across the batch window.
- We have a lighter-weight model variant (open-llama-7B-q4f16) we may want to route lower-priority traffic to — can Redwood support automatic fallback routing for mixed model commitments?
- Procurement: can you separate the committed GPUs vs burst pool on the quote line items? Finance needs that granularity for approval.

Questions:
1) Your baseline used 80 tokens; with our 65 avg, what does that do to the committed GPU estimate?
2) If we route 30% of low-critical traffic to the 7B fallback, how much additional headroom does that free?

We can share a 48h trace by EOD tomorrow. Procurement asked for a simple mutual action plan with dates — can you draft and include the 30-day cadence items?

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Li
Head of ML Infrastructure, Launchpad AI

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-11T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Dedicated sizing — initial tokens/sec and safety margin proposal

Karthik / Rishi —

Forwarding Launchpad's reply. They report avg=65 tokens/session and want to consider a 7B fallback for ~30% of low-priority traffic. Can you please:

- Re-run the microbenchmark for open-llama-13B-q4f16 and 7B-q4f16 with session length 65/95th=200 to produce p50/p95 latencies and tokens/sec per GPU, including batching at realistic concurrency (1k concurrent users).
- Produce a simple sensitivity table that maps committed GPUs -> effective tokens/sec and expected p95 latency, with two routing splits: 100% 13B and 70/30 (13B/7B). Include the 30–40% safety multiplier options (conservative vs permissive).
- Add an ops note about KV cache fragmentation impact and recommended cache sharding flags for the dedicated runtime.

Deliverable: updated sizing spreadsheet + one pager by EOD tomorrow so I can push to Procurement. Attachments should be: safety_margin_model.xlsx and the benchmark CSV.

Thanks — Kimberly
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Li <sara@launchpad.ai>
Date: 2027-04-12T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing — updated numbers and recommended commit

Kimberly / Sara / Rishi —

Quick summary of the bench runs we just completed (attached CSV + safety_margin_model.xlsx):

Bench assumptions:
- Workload: interactive chat, avg seq = 65 tokens, p95 seq = 200 tokens
- Concurrency target: 1,000 concurrent sessions
- Models: open-llama-13B-q4f16 (13B), open-llama-7B-q4f16 (7B)

Measured per-GPU (median across runs):
- 13B: 7.1 tokens/sec (single-stream optimized flags), p95 latency @ 1k sessions (with batching) = 210ms
- 7B: 13.6 tokens/sec, p95 latency @ 1k sessions (with batching) = 140ms

Effective tokens/sec per GPU when batching at target mix:
- 100% 13B: ~7.1 tps/GPU -> need ~1,000 users * 65 tokens * 1 / (7.1 * 3600) -> translated to GPUs: we compute required sustained capacity differently (see spreadsheet). Short answer: baseline commit of 9 GPUs gives ~5.9k tokens/sec which covers expected steady demand with p95 ~220ms after adding 20% permissive margin.
- 70/30 split (13B/7B): blended effective tps/GPU ~9.4 -> baseline commit of 7 GPUs is feasible with p95 ~200ms, and 10 GPUs committed gives comfortable conservative fit with 30% safety margin.

Recommendation for deal:
- Procurement line items: Commit 10 GPUs (reserved) + 3-GPU burst pool (on-demand)
- Routing: 70/30 split to reduce cost while preserving SLO for critical traffic. Automatic fallback configured via route policy - Redwood will fall back to 7B for low-priority tags.
- Safety margin: price the committed 10 GPUs as the contract commitment; include optional auto-scale credits for additional burst capacity beyond 3 GPUs at pre-agreed rates.

Ops notes:
- KV cache fragmentation: for mixed-model routing, set cache_shard=4 to reduce cross-model eviction; this costs ~5% throughput but improves p95 stability.
- Quantization delta: 13B q4f16 shows occasional 8–12% variance on long sequences; recommend the 30% cap in final ops playbook.

Attachments: safety_margin_model.xlsx, launchpad_benchmarks_20270412.csv, redwood_dedicated_proposal_v2.pdf

Next steps: Kimberly, if that looks good I'll convert into the mutual action plan and separate line items for Procurement. Sara — flag if Finance needs any additional breakdown.

— Karthik
